summary: iteration_82 backend-only verification of the Vertex AI Gemini 2.5 Flash hardening round. Re-ran test_iter81_vertex_ai.py (extended from 25 -> 40 tests) and test_iter81_api_e2e.py (6 tests). The iteration_81 failure TestJsonFenceParsing::test_prose_before_fence now PASSES thanks to the shared _extract_json() helper; I also added direct unit tests for _extract_json (7 cases: fenced/bare/prose-before+after/outer-list-vs-braces/fence-without-tag/invalid/empty) - all pass. Verified the recoverable _vertex_client_failed_at latch (5-min TTL, recovers after expiry), the _THINKING_BUDGETS mapping (high=16384, medium=4096, default 0) and its forwarding into _vertex_generate_sync, max_output_tokens=65535, and unquoted GCP_PROJECT_ID/GCP_LOCATION in backend/.env. Backend logs confirm info-level '[AI] served by gemini-2.5-flash (fallback model would have been o4-mini)' entries during the API e2e run, with ZERO '[Vertex AI]' fallback warnings. Two test-code (not app) breakages caused by the new reasoning_effort parameter were fixed in the test file. ONE genuine intermittent defect found: analyze_meeting() occasionally (~8%, 2 failures in ~25 live runs) receives an unterminated/invalid JSON body from Gemini and dead-ends on the 'Analysis could not be parsed' placeholder with NO OpenAI fallback or retry.

critical.issue: INTERMITTENT (~8%: 2 fails in ~25 live runs, reproduced twice via pytest TestAnalyzeMeeting::test_analysis_served_by_gemini_without_openai_fallback): Gemini returns a response that begins '```json\n{"summary": ...' but is unterminated/invalid, _extract_json raises JSONDecodeError, and analyze_meeting returns the static placeholder {'summary': 'Analysis could not be parsed...', actions: [], risks: [], all mappings: []}. No retry and no OpenAI fallback is attempted because the parse happens AFTER _ai_chat returns, so the user silently gets an empty analysis. Fix: on JSONDecodeError, retry once (or call _openai_chat directly) before giving up; and raise inside _vertex_generate_sync when finish_reason != STOP (e.g. MAX_TOKENS) so _ai_chat's existing fallback path triggers.

minor.issue: Parse-failure log truncates the raw response to 500 chars and _extract_json's JSONDecodeError always reports 'line 1 column 1 (char 0)', so the real cause (truncation vs bad escaping vs finish_reason) is undiagnosable from logs. Log finish_reason/usage_metadata and the response tail (or full body at DEBUG).
finish_reason is computed but only used in the empty-text error message; a MAX_TOKENS/SAFETY truncated-but-non-empty response is returned as if successful.

File is 1967 lines - exceeds the 700-line guideline; consider splitting provider plumbing (_ai_chat/_gemini_chat/_openai_chat/_extract_json) into utils/ai_client.py and keeping prompts/features separate.

action_items: HIGH: Make JSON parse failure recoverable in analyze_meeting (retry / explicit OpenAI fallback) instead of returning the empty 'Analysis could not be parsed' placeholder - reproduced ~8% of live runs.
MEDIUM: Raise in _vertex_generate_sync when candidate finish_reason is not STOP so truncated responses trigger the existing OpenAI fallback.
MEDIUM: Improve parse-failure logging (finish_reason, usage_metadata, longer/complete response body).
critical_code_review_comments: _extract_json() itself is now solid: verified fenced, bare, prose-before, prose-after, prose-around-unfenced, fence-without-json-tag, outer-list-vs-inner-braces, invalid and empty inputs. Its weakness is only that callers treat JSONDecodeError as terminal.

_get_vertex_client() TTL latch behaves correctly: latch set on missing config, suppressed for 300s even after config returns, and recovers once the TTL elapses (verified by monkeypatching the timestamp).

reasoning_effort -> ThinkingConfig plumbing verified end-to-end; unknown/None efforts safely map to thinking_budget=0. Live calls showed thoughts_token_count 2.3k-5.5k with reasoning_effort='high' and STOP finish reason, total ~20-24k tokens - well inside the 65535 output cap.

success_rate.backend: 98% (45/46: 39/40 vertex suite + 6/6 api e2e; the single failure is the intermittent Gemini JSON-truncation dead-end)

seed_data_creation: None - reused existing seeded meetings via tests/_iter79_login.py MFA bypass in the API e2e suite.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run both suites with `python -m pytest tests/test_iter81_vertex_ai.py tests/test_iter81_api_e2e.py -p no:randomly -n 0` from /app/backend (~4 min, real LLM calls; the --count flag is unavailable, pytest-repeat not installed). Test-file fixes made this round: stub/boom signatures now accept reasoning_effort (the new param broke 5 tests as a pure test-code issue), stale aimod._vertex_client_failed -> _vertex_client_failed_at, plus new classes TestExtractJsonHelper, TestVertexClientLatchTtl, TestThinkingBudgets and 2 extra fence cases. The only remaining failure, TestAnalyzeMeeting::test_analysis_served_by_gemini_without_openai_fallback, is FLAKY (~8%) and model-side - re-run several times; probe scripts _iter82_probe*.py capture finish_reason/usage/raw text for diagnosis (they write bad raw payloads to /tmp/iter82_bad_*.txt).

flaky_tests.cause: Gemini returned unterminated/invalid JSON; app has no retry/fallback at the parse layer

rca_of_the_issue: iteration_81's test_prose_before_fence failure is genuinely fixed: _extract_json first strips a closed ```json fence via regex, then attempts json.loads, then falls back to outer-bracket extraction preferring the earliest of the '{...}' / '[...]' candidates - so leading/trailing prose and bare JSON all parse. The remaining failure is different: on ~8% of live analyze_meeting calls Gemini emits a fence-opened but never-closed / invalid JSON body. _extract_json correctly raises JSONDecodeError, but analyze_meeting's except-block returns a hard-coded empty analysis placeholder rather than retrying or invoking the OpenAI fallback (the fallback only wraps transport/API errors inside _ai_chat, not parse errors). Instrumented probes (7 consecutive runs) showed finish_reason=STOP, thoughts 2.3k-5.5k tokens, candidates 3.5k-5.5k tokens - well below the 65535 cap - so this is model-side output non-determinism, not a token-limit misconfiguration; it must be handled with a parse-level retry/fallback.
